tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Each `cua_repl.js` call opens or continues a browser activity. Keep consecutive calls together. The activity stays open across messages until you emit completion commentary.

**Manual takeover takes priority over the table below.** For a required manual browser step, call the documented takeover API before asking the user to act, unless takeover is already pending. Explain the required step in your final reply. Tab marking alone does not transfer control. While waiting for the user to finish and return control, emit no completion and make no CUA calls, even when answering side questions. The takeover API returning does not end this wait. When the user returns or unblocks you, resume browser work and apply the table. If they cancel, replace, or no longer need the browser work, close the activity before answering, even without another CUA call.

Completion is a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Never put it in a tool call or final reply. Use 3–6 words starting with a past-tense verb to describe the observed outcome. Omit identifiers.

After a user cancels pending browser work: commentary `::browser-complete{title="Stopped browser work"}`, then the final acknowledgement. No browser call is needed.

For an open browser activity:

| Next action                                   | Required output order                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Another CUA call                              | Continue without completion.                                                              |
| A non-CUA tool, final reply, or chat question | Finish required tab marking, emit completion, then take that action in the same response. |

With no open activity, emit no completion. Later CUA use requires a fresh completion at the next table boundary.

If you need a one-time sign-in code, information, or confirmation from the user, follow the table and ask in chat. One-time code entry alone does not require takeover. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Feature Specification Standard

This standard defines the quality bar for high-level feature specifications
before implementation begins.

## Core Principle

A feature specification passes if a competent engineer (or fresh AI session) who
is unfamiliar with the codebase can understand the proposed feature, the
business motivation, and the design trade-offs, and confirm that all major risks
and alternatives have been addressed.

## The Alternatives Rule

The specification must include a **mandatory evaluation of alternatives**. It
fails this standard if it proposes a single path without proving that other
viable designs were considered and rejected for specific, documented reasons
(including, but not limited to, complexity, cost, performance, or scalability).
Rejection rationales must state concrete technical or scope trade-offs and must
not attribute a rejection to a maintainer without linking their issue,
discussion, or PR.

## Risks & Limits

The specification must explicitly call out its own constraints. It must identify
potential failure modes, security implications, scalability limits, and how they
will be mitigated.

## Requirements (Non-Exhaustive Examples)

The specification must detail these areas if applicable to the changes:

*   **Problem Statement**: The business or user problem being solved.
*   **Goals & Non-Goals**: What the feature will and will not deliver.
*   **Proposed Architecture**: Component layout, data flows, and ecosystem
    integration.
*   **Alternatives Considered**: Rejected options and rationale for rejection.
*   **Risks & Mitigations**: Identified security, scalability, or complexity
    risks.

# Frame Management REST API working hypothesis

Expose the Spring Boot REST API under /api/frames over the existing PostgreSQL frame and frame_version schema. The inventory list, detail/edit, and audit history views consume the API.

- GET /api/frames returns current versions only, ordered by frameId, with zero-based page and size. Default size is 25 and maximum is 50. Invalid parameters produce 400. Search and filtering are deferred.
- GET /api/frames/{frameId} returns the current version and the versionId needed for the next write. Unknown or deleted IDs return 404.
- GET /api/frames/{frameId}/history returns all versions ordered by valid_from descending. Deletion preserves history. Define the response for an unknown ID.
- POST /api/frames validates input, creates the stable frame and first current version with MANUAL_CREATE, and returns 201 with a Location header and created body. Any reused ID returns 409, even after soft deletion. The stable frame ID is permanently reserved.
- PUT /api/frames/{frameId} requires expectedVersionId. Compare it to the current version under a lock on the stable frame row, close that version, and append a new current version with MANUAL_EDIT. Return 409 for a stale version.
- DELETE /api/frames/{frameId} accepts optional expectedVersionId, returns 409 on mismatch, and on success returns 204. Close the current version and set its change_source to MANUAL_DELETE without inserting a successor.
- Close and append in one PostgreSQL transaction. The existing schema keeps closed version intervals positive and permits at most one current version. A V2 Flyway migration adds change_source. Existing rows keep null until an operation records a change source.
- Validate bodies and path/query parameters with Jakarta Validation, including required fields, coordinate and numeric bounds, and enum values where defined. A global Spring MVC exception handler returns consistent 400 errors with field details, 404 for missing frames, and 409 for conflicts.
- Unit-test service transitions, version conflicts and deletion. Use Spring Boot HTTP integration tests against PostgreSQL with Flyway enabled to cover all endpoints and expected success/error statuses.
- Scope is backend and tests. The Global Linear board already contains a parent and four sub-tasks.

- Load `tokens.css` before `styles.css`. The first defines fonts, color, typography, spacing and elevation. The second styles the shell, buttons, fields, inventory tables, chips and timelines. `[tokens.css::root]` `[styles.css:.app]` `[styles.css:.btn]` `[styles.css:.field]` `[styles.css:.tbl]` `[styles.css:.chip]` `[styles.css:.timeline]`
- `window.FRAME_DATA` exposes sample frames, status metadata, fixture-derived filter options and map pin positions. The shell exposes shared browser components including `Icon`, `Rail`, `Topbar`, `FrameMap`, `Timeline` and `ExternalIdsTable`. `[data.jsx:window.FRAME_DATA]` `[shell.jsx:Object.assign]`
- Direction A offers a filter sidebar and table or map, with separate detail and edit screens and a history tab. Its text search includes external ID values. Direction B keeps a searchable, site-filtered list beside a pane that switches between map, detail, edit and history. `[direction-a.jsx:DirA]` `[direction-a.jsx:DirA_Search]` `[direction-a.jsx:DirA_Detail]` `[direction-b.jsx:DirB]`
- The new frame wizard has five steps from Basics through Review. The master data rail opens regions and towns, site types, formats and external ID systems via `md-regions`, `md-sites`, `md-formats` and `md-extids`. `[master-data.jsx:NewFrameScreen]` `[master-data.jsx:MD_CONTENT]` `[shell.jsx:Rail]`

## Invariants

- The app starts in Direction A with comfortable density and the search screen. Switching direction returns to the frame search screen. Shortcuts 1–4 select screens and A/B selects direction when focus is outside inputs, textareas and selects. `[app.jsx:DEFAULT_TWEAKS]` `[app.jsx:App]`
- Both directions initialize selection to `FRM-00214` and fall back to the first fixture if the selection cannot be resolved. Direction A uses the same filtered results for its table and map. Direction B retains its list controls while switching panes. `[direction-a.jsx:DirA]` `[direction-a.jsx:DirA_Search]` `[direction-b.jsx:DirB]`
- The wizard starts with `draft` status and the first region, site type and technology from `window.FRAME_DATA`. `[master-data.jsx:NewFrameScreen]`

## Side Effects

- Script initialization fills empty fixture histories with sample events and publishes the shared data and components as browser globals. `[data.jsx:FRAMES.forEach]` `[data.jsx:window.FRAME_DATA]` `[shell.jsx:Object.assign]` `[direction-a.jsx:window.DirA]` `[direction-b.jsx:window.DirB]` `[master-data.jsx:Object.assign]`
- Frame edit Save changes and Cancel both return to detail. Save as draft and the external ID link, edit and unlink controls have no handlers. These controls leave the fixture records and history unchanged. `[direction-a.jsx:DirA_Edit]` `[direction-b.jsx:DirB_Edit]` `[direction-b.jsx:DirB]` `[shell.jsx:ExternalIdsTable]`
- Create frame passes the in-memory draft to `onCreate(draft)`. The app returns to the frame section without adding a record. Master data Create and Save changes only close the drawer. Delete has no handler. `[master-data.jsx:NewFrameScreen]` `[master-data.jsx:MDDrawer]` `[master-data.jsx:MasterDataScreen]` `[app.jsx:App]`
- Tweak changes update React state, send `__edit_mode_set_keys` to the parent window and dispatch `tweakchange` in the current window. The panel listens for host activation and deactivation, reads `deck-stage.railVisible` from local storage, and sends `__deck_rail_visible` to the current window when toggled. These hooks make no local storage writes. `[tweaks-panel.jsx:useTweaks]` `[tweaks-panel.jsx:TweaksPanel]`

## Verification

Run this command from the repository root.

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory design-system
```

Open [the local prototype](http://localhost:8000/Frame%20Inventory.html) in a browser that can reach the CDN scripts. Use the A/B controls to switch directions, filter the frames, and open a frame from the list and map. Open the edit screen and confirm that Save changes returns to detail with the fixture values. Complete the New frame wizard and open a master data drawer to check that Create returns to the existing fixture view.

## Content fundamentals

- Use a factual, operational tone and second person where an action is required. Examples include “Add a frame” and “Pick from master data”.
- Use sentence case for buttons, headings and columns. Keep acronyms such as OOH, CMS and DSP uppercase.
- Keep labels short and put longer help below them in `--text-secondary`. Prefer inline help.
- Keep product surfaces free of emoji. Use dots and chips for status.
- Give numbers context, such as `412 m`, `10s · 6/min` and `FRM-00214`. Use a middle dot to separate related details.

## Visual foundations

- Use the Inter type scale. Body copy defaults to `--fs-body2` (14px), with 13px for dense UI elements. Use weights 500–600 to distinguish headings.
- Use `--blue-1000` (#046AC4) for primary actions. Use near-white and cool neutrals for the canvas, with green, red and orange for status.
- Place white cards on the near-white canvas. Use 1px `--border-subtle` borders on resting surfaces and `--border-default` on inputs. Reserve elevation for popovers and drawers.
- Use `--radius` (4px) for inputs and buttons, `--radius-lg` (8px) for surfaces, and `--radius-pill` (999px) for chips and pills.
- Use an 8px spacing base. Use `--sp-2` or `--sp-3` for typical gaps of 16px or 24px.
- Use a subtle tint on hover and a darker tint when pressed. Keep control dimensions steady and reserve motion for state changes.
- Keep app chrome focused on text and data.

## Iconography

Use the inline SVGs in `shell.jsx` as the reference for new glyphs. Use a 1.8px stroke, round caps and joins, and `currentColor`. Size domain glyphs at 16–24px. `[shell.jsx:Icon]` `[shell.jsx:SiteIcon]`

- Actions and navigation include `search`, `plus`, `pencil`, `trash`, `chev`, `chevL`, `filter`, `download`, `upload`, `map`, `list`, `pin`, `history`, `more`, `link`, `warn`, `info`, `check` and `x`.
- Domain glyphs include `station`, `road`, `airport`, `mall`, `bus`, `frame`, `dash`, `cog`, `report`, `school` and `globe`.

## Caveats

The system covers Frame Inventory operational screens. Marketing surfaces and dark mode are outside its scope.

`tokens.css` loads local TrueType Inter files at weights 400, 500, 600 and 700. Keep the relative `fonts/` paths when reusing the stylesheet. The font stack falls back to the platform sans serif and Arial. `[tokens.css:@font-face]` `[tokens.css:--font-sans]`
